identity.name: Kingdom of Naples
alt_names: Kingdom of Sicily on this side of the Faro

land.text: the mainland that Charles of Anjou kept after the 1282 rebellion lost him the island of Sicily

predecessors.note: Cliopatria starts the Naples row in 1285 and gives the Kingdom of Sicily row only a 548 km2 piece in 1279-1284; the page dates the kingdom from 1282.

land.text: Treaty of Granada: Louis would receive the northern regions, including Abruzzo and Terra di Lavoro; Naples itself surrendered to the French in August 1501

successors.note: Cliopatria draws the Naples area inside the Kingdom of France shape in 1502-1506.

land.text: Treaty of Granada: Ferdinand would receive Calabria and the Apulian territories of Terra di Bari and Terra di Otranto

successors.note: Basilicata, Principato and Capitanata were left unassigned and disputed; by the end of 1503 Ferdinand held the whole kingdom, later the Spanish viceroyalty of Naples (a state for the additions batch, see notes).

correction.text: the 1285 shape unchanged, applied to 1282-1284: the mainland Charles of Anjou kept after losing the island of Sicily

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1282-1284: Cliopatria has no Naples row before 1285 although the page dates the kingdom from 1282 ('established by the War of the Sicilian Vespers (1282-1302)'; Charles of Anjou 'kept the mainland'). The page gives no infobox area, so the 68,688 km2 of the 1285 shape cannot be compared.

correction.text: the 1285 shape unchanged; holds 1285-1441 only (1442-1458 the land is Aragonese, 'part of the Crown of Aragon 1442-1458')

keyframe_review.note: Shape unchanged but its years change: it holds 1285-1441 and again from 1459. The page gives 'part of the Crown of Aragon 1442-1458' and 'In 1442, Alfonso V conquered the Kingdom of Naples', so 1442-1458 is drawn in the Crown of Aragon's colour (ledger loss 1442, gain 1458); Cliopatria's row ends 1449 and its Crown of Aragon row apparently absorbs the land only from 1450 (area 184,924 to 243,504 km2). No infobox area on the page.

68,688 km2, the same outline: the kingdom restored to a separate Aragonese king after 1458 ('Naples was inherited by Ferdinand I, Alfonso's illegitimate son'). The page lists Abruzzo, Calabria and Apulia among the modern regions; it gives no area. The 1495 French interlude has no gap in Cliopatria.

Same outline, 1497-1501: Frederick IV's kingdom until the French and Spanish partition ('In 1501, he occupied Naples and partitioned the kingdom with Ferdinand of Aragon'); the shape ends in 1501 as the page's 'sovereign state 1458-1501'.

region.text: the mainland south of the Papal States (Abruzzo, Campania, Apulia, Basilicata, Calabria)

ledger.note: 1282: after the Sicilian Vespers Charles of Anjou loses the island of Sicily but keeps the mainland, the Kingdom of Naples. 'After the 1282 rebellion, Charles of Anjou lost the island of Sicily but kept the mainland, which became known as the Kingdom of Naples'; infobox 'Established: 1282, War of the Sicilian Vespers (1282-1302)'. The page gives no month and no boundary; the land is the Cliopatria 1285 shape.

1302: the Peace of Caltabellotta fixes the name Kingdom of Sicily Citra Farum. 'the Peace of Caltabellotta (1302) provided that the name of the kingdom would be the Kingdom of Sicily Citra Farum'; the page adds that 'Kingdom of Naples' was the colloquial name, not used officially.

region.text: the whole kingdom, conquered by Alfonso V

ledger.note: 1442: Alfonso V of Aragon conquers the Kingdom of Naples and holds it with Sicily as a dependency of Aragon. 'In 1442, Alfonso V conquered the Kingdom of Naples and unified Sicily and Naples once again as dependencies of Aragon'; infobox 'part of the Crown of Aragon 1442-1458'. Cliopatria moves the land into its Crown of Aragon row only in 1450.

region.text: the whole kingdom inherited by Ferdinand I

ledger.note: 1458: Alfonso V dies and Naples passes to his illegitimate son Ferdinand I as a separate kingdom. 'Naples was inherited by Ferdinand I, Alfonso's illegitimate son'; infobox 'Sovereign state 1282-1442 and 1458-1501'. The page names the war that followed only as '(1458-1462)'. Cliopatria's Naples row resumes in 1459.

region.text: the kingdom, held by the French from February 1495

ledger.note: 1495: Charles VIII takes Naples. 'Alfonso II decided to abdicate in favor of his more-popular son Ferdinand' (22 January 1495); 'The French army captured Naples without a fight' (22 February 1495) and Charles was crowned king of Naples; he left Montpensier as viceroy with a garrison and marched north on 20 May 1495. (Reviewer eu-13-i: type changed from contest_start to occupation_start: the page says Charles 'occupied Naples without a fight', and kingdom-of-france records an occupation_start of this kingdom in 1495.)

region.text: the kingdom, held by the French from February 1495

ledger.note: 1495: the Aragonese return. 'The Neapolitan-Aragonese troops defeated the French garrison of Naples' on 6-7 July 1495, letting Ferdinand II return; the French in the castle held out until 8 December 1495. Cliopatria draws no gap. (Reviewer eu-13-i: type changed from contest_end to occupation_end, mirroring kingdom-of-france's occupation_end.)

region.text: Calabria and the Apulian territories of Terra di Bari and Terra di Otranto

ledger.note: 1501: the French and Spanish armies over-run the kingdom; Ferdinand's share is Calabria, Terra di Bari and Terra di Otranto. Treaty of Granada, 11 November 1500: 'Ferdinand would receive Calabria and the Apulian territories of Terra di Bari and Terra di Otranto'; 'Summer 1501: the French and Spanish forces quickly over-ran the kingdom'. The month of the Spanish occupation is not on the page; the treaty leaves Basilicata, Principato and Capitanata unassigned.

region.text: Naples, Terra di Lavoro and Abruzzo, the share of Louis XII

ledger.note: 1501: Capua falls on 24 July and Frederick surrenders Naples to the French in August. 'On 24 July, the French army captured Capua'; 'Frederick surrendered Naples to the French' (August 1501); Louis XII's share was 'the northern regions, including Abruzzo and Terra di Lavoro'.

region.text: the whole kingdom partitioned between France and Aragon

ledger.note: 1501: the Aragonese kingdom of Naples ends when Frederick gives up the capital to Louis XII; exiled to France, he dies in 1504. The page does not call this an abdication.

wars.name: War of the Sicilian Vespers

zones.text: the island of Sicily, lost by Charles of Anjou in 1282

wars.outcome: Charles of Anjou lost the island and kept the mainland, the Kingdom of Naples; the Peace of Caltabellotta (1302) set the mainland kingdom's name as Kingdom of Sicily Citra Farum.
wars.note: The page opened does not name the Aragonese side; the island's later holders are the Crown of Aragon and Kingdom of Sicily dossiers.

wars.name: Italian War of 1494-1495

zones.text: the kingdom of Naples, taken in February 1495

wars.outcome: Charles VIII captured Naples without a fight on 22 February 1495 after Alfonso II abdicated for Ferdinand II, left for Lombardy on 20 May and the Aragonese defeated the French garrison on 6-7 July 1495; the castle held out to 8 December 1495. Ferrantino died in 1496 and his uncle Frederick IV succeeded (Kingdom of Naples page).
wars.note: The Kingdom of Naples page calls the war only by the years quoted.

wars.name: French and Spanish partition and conquest of Naples
wars.outcome: Treaty of Granada (11 November 1500) partitioned the kingdom; Capua fell 24 July 1501 and Frederick surrendered Naples in August; the allies fell out over Basilicata, Principato and Capitanata, war resumed in late 1502 and by the end of 1503 the French were expelled and Ferdinand held the whole kingdom.
wars.note: Only the 1500-1501 stage falls inside this state's life; the French-Aragonese war of 1502-1503 is for the successors' dossiers.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a treaty line; the land frontier with the Papal States was not read, so every border is drawn from Cliopatria's approximate outline.

notes: Pages opened: 3 against a budget of 1-2 (the third, Italian War of 1494-1495, was opened for the Florence dossier and used here to date the French interlude). Cliopatria's Kingdom of Naples (1285-1449, 1459-1501) is one outline of 68,688 km2 throughout; the Wikipedia infobox gives no area, so the factor-of-two check could not be made. The Wikipedia article treats the Kingdom of Naples as lasting to 1816; Cliopatria and this dossier end it at the 1501 partition, so the Spanish viceroyalty (1503/1504-1707), the Austrian viceroyalty (1707-1734) and the 1734 Bourbon kingdom need their own dossiers (kingdom-of-naples-bourbon and kingdom-of-naples-napoleonic already exist; the viceroyalties are for batch eu-13-x). Cliopatria draws the Naples area in the Kingdom of France row for 1502-1506 and in the Crown of Aragon row from 1507. The 1442-1458 Aragonese interval is a gain/loss pair with the Crown of Aragon; the kingdom was never extinct in law, only a dependency. Page silent: the Battle of Cerignola and Garigliano (not on the pages), the 1458-1462 war's name and zones, the French withdrawal from Naples other than the castle's 8 December 1495 (Kingdom page: 'soon forced to withdraw'). The Italian War of 1499-1504 article (the titles tried did not load) could fill the rest.
